original:
श्लोक ४-५ ]
* साधक-संजीवनी *
५०३
वास्तविकताका अनुभव करनेसे वह माना हुआ सम्बन्ध | प्राप्त और परमात्मा प्राप्त होनेपर भी अप्राप्त प्रतीत हो रहे
मिट जाता है।
।
विशेष बात
जैसे गुरु-शिष्यका सम्बन्ध होता है, तो इसमें गुरु
शिष्यको अपना शिष्य मानता है । शिष्य गुरुको अपना गुरु
मानता है। इस प्रकार गुरु अलग है और शिष्य अलग है
अर्थात् उन दोनोंकी अलग-अलग सत्ता दीखती है । परन्तु
उन दोनोंके सम्बन्धसे एक तीसरी सत्ता प्रतीत होने लग
जाती है, जिसको 'सम्बन्धकी सत्ता' कहते हैं * । ऐसे ही
साक्षात् परमात्माके अंश जीवने शरीर-संसारके साथ अपना
सम्बन्ध मान लिया है। इस सम्बन्धके कारण एक तीसरी
सत्ता प्रतीत होने लग जाती है, जिसको 'मैं' - पन कहते
हैं। सम्बन्धकी यह सत्ता ('मैं' - पन) केवल मानी हुई है,
वास्तवमें है नहीं। जीव भूलसे इस माने हुए सम्बन्धको
सत्य मान लेता है अर्थात् इसमें सद्भाव कर लेता है और
बँध जाता है। इस प्रकार जीव संसारसे नहीं, प्रत्युत संसारसे
माने हुए सम्बन्धसे ही बँधता है ।
हैं । संसारसे माना हुआ सम्बन्ध टूटते ही परमात्माके
वास्तविक सम्बन्धका अथवा संसारकी अप्राप्ति और
परमात्माकी प्राप्तिका अनुभव हो जाता है ।
'मैं' - पनको मिटानेके लिये साधक प्रकृति और
प्रकृतिके कार्यको न तो अपना स्वरूप समझे, न उससे
कुछ मिलनेकी इच्छा रखे और न ही अपने लिये कुछ
करे । जो कुछ करे, वह सब केवल संसारकी सेवाके लिये
ही करता रहे। तात्पर्य है कि जो कुछ प्रकृतिजन्य पदार्थ
हैं, उन सबकी संसारके साथ एकता है; अतः उनको केवल
संसारका मानकर संसारकी ही सेवामें लगाता रहे । इससे
क्रिया और पदार्थोंका प्रवाह संसारकी तरफ हो जाता है
और अपना स्वरूप अवशिष्ट रह जाता है अर्थात् अपने
स्वरूपका बोध हो जाता है। यह कर्मयोग हुआ। ज्ञानयोगमें
विवेक - विचारपूर्वक प्रकृतिके कार्य पदार्थों और क्रियाओंसे
सर्वथा सम्बन्ध-विच्छेद करनेपर स्वरूपका बोध हो जाता
है । इस प्रकार जडके सम्बन्धसे जो अहंता ('मैं' - पन)
पैदा हुई थी, उसकी निवृत्ति हो जाती है।
भक्तियोगमें ‘मैं केवल भगवान्‌का हूँ और केवल
भगवान् ही मेरे हैं तथा मैं शरीर - संसारका नहीं हूँ और
शरीर - संसार मेरे नहीं हैं' - ऐसी दृढ़ मान्यता करके भक्त
संसारसे विमुख होकर केवल भगवत्परायण हो जाता है,
जिससे संसारका सम्बन्ध स्वतः टूट जाता है और अहंताकी
निवृत्ति हो जाती है।
गुरु और शिष्यमें तो दोनोंकी अलग-अलग सत्ता है
और दोनों एक-दूसरेसे सम्बन्ध मानते हैं; परन्तु जीव
(चेतन) और संसार (जड) – इन दोनोंमें केवल एक
जीवकी ही वास्तविक सत्ता है और यही भूलसे संसारके
साथ अपना सम्बन्ध मानता है । संसार प्रतिक्षण नष्ट हो रहा
है; अतः उससे माना हुआ सम्बन्ध भी प्रतिक्षण स्वतः नष्ट |
हो रहा है। ऐसा होते हुए भी जबतक संसारमें सुख प्रतीत
होता है, तबतक उससे माना हुआ सम्बन्ध स्थायी प्रतीत
होता है। तात्पर्य यह है कि संसारसे माना हुआ सम्बन्ध
सुखासक्तिपर ही टिका हुआ है । संसारसे सुखासक्तिपूर्वक
माने
हुए सम्बन्धके कारण ही संसार अप्राप्त होनेपर भी
परिशिष्ट भाव – जब चेतन अपरा प्रकृतिके साथ तादात्म्य कर लेता है अर्थात् 'अहम्' के साथ एक होकर
अपनेको 'मैं हूँ' ऐसा मान लेता है, तब वह जीवरूप बनी हुई 'परा प्रकृति' कहलाता है । ' अहम्' (मैं) से इधर
जगत् (अपरा प्रकृति) है और उधर परमात्मा हैं । परन्तु जीव उन परमात्माको स्वीकार न करके, प्रत्युत उनकी अपरा
प्रकृतिको स्वीकार करके उसको जगत्-रूपसे धारण कर लेता है और जन्म-मरणरूप बन्धनमें पड़ जाता है।
-
इस प्रकार कर्मयोग, ज्ञानयोग और भक्तियोग — इन
तीनोंमेंसे किसी एकका भी ठीक अनुष्ठान करनेपर जडतासे
सर्वथा सम्बन्ध विच्छेद होकर परमात्मतत्त्वकी प्राप्ति हो
जाती है ।
‘अपरेयमितस्त्वन्याम्’– अपरासे अन्य परा है और परासे अन्य अपरा है। अपरा 'अन्य' अर्थात् विजातीय
है। अन्यको पकड़नेसे ही परा 'जीव' बनी है— 'जीवभूताम्' ।
-
अपरा (परिवर्तनशील) और परा (अपरिवर्तनशील ) – दोनों ही भगवान्‌की प्रकृतियाँ अर्थात् शक्तियाँ हैं, स्वभाव हैं
भगवान्‌की शक्ति होनेसे दोनों भगवान् से अभिन्न हैं; क्योंकि शक्तिमान् के बिना शक्तिकी स्वतन्त्र सत्ता नहीं होती । जैसे
*
।
गुरु-शिष्यके सम्बन्धमें गुरुका काम केवल शिष्यका हित करना है और शिष्यका काम केवल गुरुकी सेवा करना है।
इस प्रकार संसारमें माने हुए जितने भी सम्बन्ध हैं, सब केवल एक-दूसरेका हित या सेवा करनेके लिये ही हैं, अपने लिये नहीं ।
english:
Shloka 4-5]

503
The experience of reality makes the perceived relationship (with the world) seem to be obtained and yet unobtained even after attaining the Supreme Being (Paramatma) disappears.

Special Point
Just as the relationship between a guru and a disciple is formed, in this case, the guru considers the disciple as his disciple, and the disciple considers the guru as his guru. In this way, the guru and the disciple are separate, and their separate existence is perceived. However, from their relationship, a third entity is perceived, which is called the "relationship entity". Similarly, the embodied self (jiva) has considered its relationship with the body and the world as real. Due to this relationship, a third entity is perceived, which is called the "I" (aham). This perceived "I" is only an illusion and does not exist in reality. The embodied self, due to ignorance, considers this perceived relationship as real and gets attached to it. In this way, the embodied self gets attached to the world, not the world itself, but the perceived relationship with it.

When the perceived relationship with the world breaks, the experience of the real relationship with the Supreme Being or the realization of the unattainability of the world and the attainability of the Supreme Being is obtained.

To eliminate the "I" (aham), the seeker should not consider nature (prakriti) and its activities as his own form, nor should he have any desire to obtain anything from it, nor should he perform any action for his own benefit. Whatever he does, he should do it only for the service of the world. This means that whatever natural objects exist, they are all connected with the world; therefore, he should consider them as belonging to the world and serve the world only. In this way, the flow of actions and objects will be towards the world, and his true form will be preserved, i.e., he will have the experience of his true form. This is the practice of karma yoga.

In the practice of jnana yoga, the seeker, through discrimination and reasoning, completely separates himself from the activities, objects, and actions of nature, and thus experiences his true form. In this way, the ignorance of the "I" (aham) created by the association with the non-self (jada) is eliminated.

In the practice of bhakti yoga, the devotee, with firm conviction, considers himself as belonging only to the Lord and the Lord as belonging only to him, and not as belonging to the body and the world. In this way, the devotee becomes detached from the world and becomes devoted to the Lord, and thus the perceived relationship with the world is automatically broken, and the ignorance of the "I" (aham) is eliminated.

In the case of the guru and the disciple, both have separate existence and consider each other as related. However, the embodied self (jiva) and the world (jada) - both have only the true existence of the embodied self, and due to ignorance, the embodied self considers its relationship with the world as real. The world is constantly being destroyed, and therefore, its perceived relationship is also constantly being destroyed. However, as long as the embodied self experiences happiness in the world, the perceived relationship with the world appears to be permanent. The reason is that the perceived relationship with the world is based on attachment to happiness.

When the embodied self, due to ignorance, considers the world as its own, it becomes attached to it, and this attachment is the root cause of birth and death. This attachment is the result of the embodied self identifying itself with the world, i.e., considering itself as "I" (aham).

In this way, the practices of karma yoga, jnana yoga, and bhakti yoga - if any one of them is practiced correctly, the ignorance of the "I" (aham) is eliminated, and the true nature of the Supreme Being is realized.

The phrase "apareyam itas tv anyam" means that the other (parā) is different from the non-self (apara), and the non-self is different from the other. The non-self is "other" (anya), i.e., foreign. The non-self becomes "jiva" (the embodied self) by grasping the other. The non-self (apara) and the other (parā) are both the powers, the nature, the qualities of the Lord. Being the powers of the Lord, both are inseparable from the Lord, because the power of the powerful one does not exist independently.

Just as the guru's work is only to benefit the disciple, and the disciple's work is only to serve the guru, in the same way, all the relationships in the world are only for the benefit or service of each other, not for one's own benefit.
